stem: One candidate plant ranks highest for vigor but grew in the brightest position in the room. What is the strongest next step before treating it as genetically superior breeding stock?
choices: Compare environmental records and replicated or progeny performance so positional advantage is separated from inherited performance
Retain the plant as the leading candidate and compare only its later flowering traits because early vigor has already been demonstrated
Repeat the vigor measurement in the same bright position so the original environmental conditions remain consistent for the selected plant
Use the observed vigor ranking together with pedigree information to estimate breeding value without additional environmental or progeny evidence
rationale: Environmental advantage can mimic genetic superiority. Repeatable phenotyping, environmental context, replication, population records, and progeny testing strengthen evidence that a selected phenotype has useful inherited value.
